title: Cue Metamodel Prototyping — scratch
content:
Goal: sketch a lightweight metamodel for cue/templates that makes it easier to compose few-shot sets, reason about brittle cases, and automate rollout checks.

High-level idea:
- 'Cue metamodel' = small typed spec layered on top of raw instructions.
  - fields: role, intent, constraints, examples[], anchor_tokens[], failure_modes[]
  - metadata: stability_score (heuristic), token_budget_hint, prospectus (short explanation)

Why: current prompt library is a flat bag of templates; when we try automated A/B rollouts the combinatorics blow up. A metamodel lets us:
- Programmatically synthesize variants (swap intent, tighten constraint, add exemplar)
- Attach regression tests to specific failure_modes and auto-run when templates change
- Provide canonical serialization for storing in S3 / eval harnesses

Concrete sketch (informal):
- role: "assistant: concise-analyst"
- intent: "summarize-research-abstract"
- constraints: ["<=3 bullets", "no hallucinations", "cite sentences"]
- examples: [ {input: "paper text...", output: "bullet1; bullet2;..."}, ... ] (examples stored as pointers to small fixtures)
- anchor_tokens: ["methodology", "results"]  // tokens to bias retrieval / KV cache priming
- failure_modes: ["omits limitations", "hallucinates numbers when table missing"]
- stability_score: "0.6"  // derived from eval runs
- token_budget_hint: "max 450 tokens"
- prospectus: "Use for product release notes summarization where concision is primary"

Notes on representation: keep as YAML/JSON lines; accept shorthand grammar for quick authoring. Provide an importer that can parse legacy templates into the metamodel with heuristics (extract examples, detect constraints).

Synthesis ops we want to support (API-level):
- expand_constraints(template, tightening=[percent]) -> variants
- swap_intent(template, intent_map) -> candidate templates
- merge_examples(setA,setB,dedupe=true) -> few-shot sets
- failure_inject(template, mode) -> negative-example variants for robustness testing

Quick experiment plan (week-by-week rough):
- W0: author 6 canonical metamodel templates from top-used templates (console, support, summaries) — pick ones with known brittle failures.
- W1: write import hooks + serializer; run basic parse on 40 legacy templates.
- W2: implement expand_constraints and merge_examples. Generate 50 variants per canonical template.
- W3: run batch eval (unit test suite + small eval set) to compute stability_score and failure_mode counts.
- W4: pick top 10 variants for human check; iterate.

Failure cases to watch for:
- Semantic drift when tightening constraints (model produces terse but wrong statements).
- Example leakage: few-shot examples that contain labels/answers that force unsafe completions.
- Token-bloating: naive merges create >2048 token prompts. Need an autoshrink that prunes examples by similarity.

Heuristics & tooling ideas:
- example-priority: score examples by representativeness (embedding cluster distance) and recency of passing evals.
- autoshrink: greedily drop least-informative example until token budget satisfied; keep at least 1 example from each cluster.
- failure-mode tags: standard taxonomy (omit, invent, misattribute, offstyle, toxic) to normalize alerts.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to map metamodel anchor_tokens to runtime KV-cache priming? (idea: expose as soft prompt key for serving runtime to prefetch embeddings)
- Storage format: single-file JSON objects vs. per-template dir with fixtures? Which plays nicer with CI diffs?
- Rollout gating: what thresholds on stability_score and failure counts should block auto-promote?
- Can we add a lightweight provenance blob so rollbacks map to the exact metamodel revision + example set?

Short checklist for next edit:
- [ ] Draft simple schema JSON + one canonical example for support-summary use case
- [ ] Hook up to eval harness GH: redwood-inference/prompts#458 and produce a tiny report (10 templates x 5 variants)
- [ ] Prototype autoshrink and test on 2 large few-shot templates
- [ ] Add a short 'authoring microguide' (do/don't) for SEs writing templates

Random quick notes:
- Use name 'cue' instead of 'prompt' in UI to signal smaller, composable building block. Might be confusing internally — flag for UX review.
- Consider tagging templates with 'safety-sensitive' to force extra eval passes.

Fragment: micro-authoring example (raw quick):
---
role: assistant: concise-reporter
intent: extract-3-bullets
constraints: ["no claims beyond text", "each bullet <= 140 chars"]
examples: [fixture://papers/acl_2023_42/section-intro.md -> "1. ...\n2. ...\n3. ..."]
anchor_tokens: ["dataset", "participants"]
failure_modes: ["adds results not present"]
prospectus: "for internal research digests"
---

Stitching this into Drive/Repo: I think this doc should land in users/ as a personal scratch first. If we get traction, move to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/prompt-metamodel/ as a canonical spec.

End scratch.
